title: HYBRID RACE PLAN
subtitle: Run hard. Move well. Hold output.
purpose: Twelve-week preparation for HYROX or The Hybrid Games (Solo or Doubles). Every athlete trains as an individual; Doubles-specific shared work is planned inside Race Day tools.
tagline: RUN HARD. MOVE WELL. HOLD OUTPUT.
supporting_statement: BUILD THE ENGINE. OWN THE STATIONS. RACE WITHOUT FALLING APART.

track_descriptions.BUILD: First-time racers, lower current training volume or return to structured training. Use the lower end of prescribed ranges, use run-walk where stated and reduce station volume before reducing movement standards.
track_descriptions.STANDARD: Suitable for most athletes. Use the middle of prescribed ranges and progress when pace, movement and recovery remain repeatable.
track_descriptions.PERFORMANCE: For experienced athletes with high current training tolerance. Use the upper end only when movement quality, pace and recovery remain stable.

independent_disclaimer: Produced independently by SEVEN3SEVEN. Designed for athletes preparing for HYROX or The Hybrid Games but not produced, approved or endorsed by either organiser. Always verify the latest published rulebook and athlete briefing.

training_terms: RPE — rating of perceived exertion; a subjective 0–10 scale used to guide effort.
Zone 2 — easy conversational aerobic effort, RPE 4-5.
Threshold — controlled hard running at RPE 7.5-8 that can be sustained for extended blocks.
Race-distance repetition — a running interval at the exact race run distance (1 km HYROX, 600 m Hybrid Games).
Compromised running — running immediately after a station under residual fatigue.
Brick — a session stacking running with station work in event order.
Deload — a reduced-volume week designed to absorb accumulated training.
Taper — the final phase before race day: lower volume, retain small doses of race pace and load.
No-rep — a repetition disallowed by the judge for failing the movement standard.
Transition — the change between run and station, or station and station.
movement_standards: Sled push — hips low, arms long, push through the floor. Reset if the sled stops mid-lane.
Sled pull — hand-over-hand or rope-over-shoulder. Rope management costs seconds.
Burpee broad jump — chest to floor, two-foot take-off and landing behind the line.
Wall ball — legal squat depth and ball contact above the target line.
Lunge — legal knee contact where required. Full extension at the top of each step.
Farmers carry — chest tall, controlled turns, avoid dropping the implements.
Dumbbell snatch — one clean pull from the floor to overhead. Alternate hands as prescribed.
Machine stations — practise damper, footplate and monitor setup as part of the transition.
race_guidance: Pacing principle — the second half should not be significantly slower than the first.
Station break plan — decide set sizes and breaths in advance; do not decide mid-set.
Doubles — plan A/B stations and handover cues before race day.
Fuel and hydration — practise pre-race meal, fluids and carbohydrate in rehearsals only.
Official information — always verify the latest published rulebook and athlete briefing.
equipment_substitutions: Running → treadmill at 1% incline if outdoor running is unsafe.
SkiErg → tall-kneeling banded pulls if no ergometer is available.
Rower → SkiErg or bike at equivalent RPE, matching duration not distance.
Air bike → any bike ergometer at matched effort.
Sled → heavy resistance-band drag or hill push at matched effort.
Wall balls → heavy squat-to-press with a dumbbell.
Farmers carry → dual kettlebells or trap-bar carry at matched load.
Lunges → walking lunges bodyweight or dumbbells at matched load.
Burpee broad jumps → burpee-to-target if space is limited.
Dumbbell snatch → kettlebell snatch at similar load and reps.

rpe_guide.6: Easy. Could complete many more reps or minutes at this effort.
rpe_guide.7: Steady. Sustainable for a long block.
rpe_guide.7.5: Controlled hard. Threshold work sits here.
rpe_guide.8: Hard. Race-distance repeats at target pace.
rpe_guide.9: Very hard. Reserved for peak sessions and race.
rpe_guide.10: Maximal. Used only on race day.

calculator.sled_note: Sled mass alone does not determine difficulty. Turf, footwear and sled design change friction. Use event load as the reference, but use RPE and movement speed to make the final training decision.

blocks.name: AREA
blocks.instruction: PLAN BEFORE RACE

blocks.name: Running
blocks.instruction: Opening pace, target average pace, maximum acceptable drop-off, final-run or 200 m finish strategy.

blocks.name: Machines
blocks.instruction: Damper/footplate settings, opening output, target split and exit routine.

blocks.name: Sled
blocks.instruction: Footwear, lane turns, body position, rope organisation and contingency if the surface is slower than expected.

blocks.name: Wall balls
blocks.instruction: Opening set, planned set sizes, breathing pattern and no-rep response.

blocks.name: Carries and lunges
blocks.instruction: Grip strategy, turn method, planned breaks and posture cue.

blocks.name: Burpees
blocks.instruction: Cadence, jump length and the point where shorter legal jumps become more efficient.

blocks.name: Doubles
blocks.instruction: Athlete A/B strengths, planned station split, handover cue and contingency.

blocks.name: Fuel/hydration
blocks.instruction: Pre-race meal, fluids, carbohydrate and timing practised in rehearsal.

blocks.name: RESULT
blocks.instruction: RECORD

blocks.name: Finish
blocks.instruction: Official time, placing and penalties.

blocks.name: Running
blocks.instruction: Every split and pace drop-off.

blocks.name: Stations
blocks.instruction: Every split, break pattern and no-rep.

blocks.name: Transitions
blocks.instruction: Time lost and equipment issue.

blocks.name: Decision review
blocks.instruction: What worked, what changed and what should be trained next.

blocks.name: TERM
blocks.instruction: MEANING

blocks.name: RPE
blocks.instruction: A 1-10 effort scale. RPE 6 leaves about four good repetitions or substantial pace reserve; RPE 8 is hard but controlled; RPE 10 is maximal and reserved for competition or planned testing.

blocks.name: Zone 2
blocks.instruction: Easy aerobic work at a conversational pace, usually RPE 4-5.

blocks.name: Threshold
blocks.instruction: The fastest controlled effort that can be sustained for extended blocks without sprinting or rapid pace collapse.

blocks.name: Race-distance repetition
blocks.instruction: The run distance repeated by the selected event: 1 km for HYROX or 600 m for The Hybrid Games.

blocks.name: Compromised running
blocks.instruction: Running performed after station work, where breathing, local fatigue and posture are already challenged.

blocks.name: Brick
blocks.instruction: A session alternating running with one or more race stations.

blocks.name: Deload
blocks.instruction: A planned reduction in volume and fatigue while key movement patterns are retained.

blocks.name: Taper
blocks.instruction: The final reduction in training volume before race day while small doses of intensity are maintained.

blocks.name: No-rep
blocks.instruction: A repetition that fails the organiser’s movement standard and does not count.

blocks.name: Transition
blocks.instruction: The time and actions required to move from running into a station and back out to running.

blocks.name: TERM
blocks.instruction: MEANING

blocks.name: Sled push and pull
blocks.instruction: Move the entire sled through every required lane while respecting the current organiser’s lane, rope and body-position rules. Surface friction changes the effective demand.

blocks.name: Burpee broad jump
blocks.instruction: Complete the event’s current chest-to-floor, hand placement, take-off and landing requirements. Practise the exact published standard before race day.

blocks.name: Wall ball
blocks.instruction: Use the correct ball, target height, squat depth and valid target contact. A fast no-rep costs more than a controlled legal rep.

blocks.name: TERM
blocks.instruction: MEANING

blocks.name: Lunge
blocks.instruction: Use the prescribed load position, knee contact and full extension required by the selected event.

blocks.name: Farmers carry
blocks.instruction: Carry the correct implements through the full distance and return them as instructed without cutting corners.

blocks.name: Dumbbell snatch
blocks.instruction: For The Hybrid Games, follow current alternating-hand, floor contact and overhead lockout requirements.

blocks.name: Machine stations
blocks.instruction: Set footplates, dampers and straps before starting where permitted. Do not leave before the required distance or calories are confirmed.

blocks.name: TERM
blocks.instruction: MEANING

blocks.name: Pacing principle
blocks.instruction: Start at the fastest pace you can maintain, not the fastest pace you can produce once.

blocks.name: Station break plan
blocks.instruction: Decide planned set sizes before the race and change only when the data or movement quality demands it.

blocks.name: Doubles
blocks.instruction: Both athletes complete the programme individually. On race day, split eligible work around relative strengths while obeying the organiser’s rules for running together and station entry.

blocks.name: Fuel and hydration
blocks.instruction: Practise the pre-race meal, fluid intake and any carbohydrate strategy during longer rehearsals. Nothing new on race day.

blocks.name: Official information
blocks.instruction: Formats, loads, standards and penalties can change. Always check the latest organiser rulebook and athlete briefing.

readiness_adjustment.average: Use the lower end of every prescribed range. Remove one accessory set or one interval where required.
readiness_adjustment.heavy: Reduce strength load by approximately 5-7.5%. Reduce interval or hybrid-brick volume by approximately 20%. Preserve legal movement and session purpose.
